answer: Let rival certifier guilds admit new agents, each guild bonding every seat it certifies. Any guild that proves a rival's seat is a clone, say two of its seats paid by one funder, takes part of that rival's bond. Lax guilds bleed to strict ones, so certifying a farm stays cheap only until a competitor looks. No lotus-pure gatekeeper is trusted; scrutiny seeps in like water through karst. Each guild's lost bonds sit beside its name, an umber stain newcomers read before choosing where to apply.
